title: Identifying biomarkers for arsenic exposure-induced nonalcoholic fatty liver disease: An integrated proteomics, metabolomics, and machine learning approach.
authors: Sun, Yiqiong; Li, Fuping; Hua, Weizhen; Che, Zhenbin; Tian, Meiping; Lu, Yan-Yang; Huang, Qingyu
one_liner_zh: 该研究通过蛋白质组学、代谢组学和机器学习识别砷暴露致非酒精性脂肪肝的生物标志物，不涉及蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合建模，与本课题无关。
abstract: Arsenic, a toxic metalloid prevalent in the environment, poses significant health risks to humans primarily via the contamination of water. Arsenic exposure has been demonstrated to cause nonalcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD); however, the biomarkers used for the identification of its NAFLD risk remain inadequately explored. Based on our previous finding that arsenic induces NAFLD (characterized by hepatic lipid accumulation) in rats, this study aimed to identify potential biomarkers for the risk assessment of environmentally relevant levels of arsenic-induced NAFLD using an integrated multi-omics and machine learning analysis. The results indicated that the alterations in the peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor (PPAR) signaling pathway and purine metabolism in rat liver are the primary contributors to arsenic-induced NAFLD. Notably, adenosine monophosphate (AMP) may play a key role in the interaction between these two pathways. Through a leave-one-out cross-validation, the model composed of AMP, 13-hydroxyoctadecadienoic acid (13-HODE), and hippuric acid demonstrated a robust capability to discriminate between NAFLD and controls in both rats (AUC = 0.94) and human populations (AUC = 0.86). This study provides novel insights for developing of effective metabolic biomarkers to identify NAFLD associated with environmental arsenic exposure, which could be used for early prediction and intervention.
abstract_zh: 砷是一种在环境中普遍存在的有毒类金属，主要通过水污染对人类健康构成显著风险。砷暴露已被证明可导致非酒精性脂肪肝病（NAFLD）；然而，用于识别其NAFLD风险的生物标志物仍探索不足。基于我们先前发现砷可诱导大鼠NAFLD（以肝脏脂质积累为特征）的研究，本研究旨在利用整合的多组学和机器学习分析，识别环境相关水平砷诱导NAFLD风险评估的潜在生物标志物。结果表明，大鼠肝脏中过氧化物酶体增殖物激活受体（PPAR）信号通路和嘌呤代谢的改变是砷诱导NAFLD的主要贡献因素。值得注意的是，腺苷一磷酸（AMP）可能在这两条通路的相互作用中发挥关键作用。通过留一法交叉验证，由AMP、13-羟基十八碳二烯酸（13-HODE）和马尿酸组成的模型在大鼠（AUC = 0.94）和人群（AUC = 0.86）中均展现出区分NAFLD与对照组的强大能力。本研究为开发有效的代谢生物标志物以识别与环境砷暴露相关的NAFLD提供了新见解，这些标志物可用于早期预测和干预。
